title: A surjective closed immersion is a universal homeomorphism
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] that is surjective on underlying sets [def-weil-surjective-morphism]; for instance $Z\subseteq X$ a finite order thickening, i.e. a closed subscheme whose quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ satisfies $\mathcal I^{n+1}=0$ for some $n\ge0$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Then $i$ is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]: for every morphism of schemes $X'\to X$ the projection $Z\times_XX'\to X'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a surjective closed immersion, hence a homeomorphism of underlying spaces. Moreover $i$ is integral (indeed finite) [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], universally injective and surjective.
